entries.test: Public reporting and negotiation records would establish whether Altman began undisclosed deal negotiations by Wednesday, before publicly supporting Amodei.
entries.note: Marcus asserts this in his own voice while crediting the New York Times; undisclosed negotiations can subsequently be documented publicly.

“It was all theatre” refers broadly to the episode; the normalization narrows it to Altman's public support. “Never had a chance” functions here as emphatic condemnation without a defined factual test.

entries.note: The factual core is checkable despite the accompanying evaluative language, especially “absurdly.”

entries.test: Procurement records, reported deal terms, and campaign finance disclosures would establish the favored party, similarity of terms, and comparative contributions.
entries.note: The normalization attributes donations to OpenAI itself, whereas the surrounding text specifically identifies Brockman's donation. That changes the donor identity.
This advocates equal treatment and judges alternatives as appearing corrupt.
The normalization drops “I think,” presenting an expressly personal assessment as an unqualified fact. “Overhypes” judges promotional excess without specifying claims or a standard.

entries.test: Public court filings, evidence of Anthropic's acquisition and use of writers' works, and settlement documents would establish the alleged unauthorized copying and the $1.5 billion settlement.
entries.note: The settlement reference gives “ripped off” a concrete copyright-related reading. A settlement alone need not establish liability.

entries.test: Dated versions of Anthropic's safety commitments and public policy announcements would establish whether it weakened its core safety pledge shortly before publication.
entries.note: “Recently” is relative to the post's February 28, 2026 publication date.
